headline: Real-World ABM Campaign Examples: Case Studies and Best Practices
keyNotes: Instead of trying to reach everyone, a smart marketing approach called "Account-Based Marketing" (ABM) focuses on treating each high-value company you want to sell to as its own unique market, tailoring everything specifically for them.

Getting the right, accurate information about who you're trying to reach is incredibly powerful; for example, SundaySky saw a huge 220% increase in how many target companies converted into customers just by using precise, human-verified data.

You can save a lot of money and improve your aim by getting all your customer information from one good source; BetterCloud saved over $100,000 by switching from multiple data providers to just one reliable source.

When your sales team and marketing team work together using the same list of target companies, it can lead to much bigger wins; Adobe found that deals influenced by their marketing efforts on LinkedIn were 161% larger when sales and marketing were aligned.
question: The article highlights how companies like Snowflake achieved a 3x meeting rate by treating specific target companies as 'markets of one' and tailoring their approach. In your own work, where do you currently treat every customer or project the same, and what might change if you started to think of each as a unique 'market of one' with its own specific needs?
